svg.title: Reading the Super Bowl Resale Curve
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-super-bowl-resale-timing-flow; chapter number: 1; chart type: process_flow; title: Reading the Super Bowl Resale Curve; subtitle: From the conference-championship spike to a game-day exit plan; caption: Five-step buying and exit sequence assembled from street brokers, StubHub commentary and resale-timing segments.; assumptions note: All figures are attributed practitioner claims for specific Super Bowl years; matchup, fan travel and leftover supply move the curve each season.; note: Sources: N.F.L Podcast (Aj09Nv4kg04 @ 00:03:31), AP Archive (NwYrOSq9-5Q @ 00:00:15; NxbqrXeuWTI @ 00:00:38), NBC10 Boston (-GwKaOFdk_M @ 00:01:24), CBS Boston (hhJFZEqMUpQ @ 00:01:02 and 00:01:16).; stages: step: 01; label: Let the conference-championship spike burn off; value: Step 1; detail: Watch prices early, wait a few days to a week for the dip, and stay out of the final rush when desperation pushes prices back up (N.F.L Podcast).; step: 02; label: Read the buyer-geography split; value: Step 2; detail: A single traveling fan base, like the Philadelphia market, kept StubHub sales 30 to 40% ahead of the prior year (AP Archive).; step: 03; label: Gauge leftover game-day supply; value: Step 3; detail: StubHub said downward movement depends on how much inventory is left on game day (AP Archive).; step: 04; label: Target the 48 to 72 hour buying window; value: Step 4; detail: Prices dip leading up to the game, then pop on game day as last-minute purchases hit the market (NBC10 Boston).; step: 05; label: Carry an exit plan or bundle a perk; value: Step 5; detail: One broker ran a pop-up near NRG Stadium with a tailgate bash for buyers; another sat on a backpack of tickets as the average slid to just over $4,400 and the low hit $1,900 (CBS Boston).
